Two things are worth knowing before you touch it. Nothing reaches students until a track is published, and every notice and the preview say so. And the four tracks the program runs today are here too, as the program's four original tracks, published from the day a site goes live; the last part of this section is what makes them different from a track you make.

The track list

One row per track, in the order they were made:

New track sits above the list. The only button a row gets sometimes is Delete, offered on a track that was never published. Delete asks first and cannot be undone, and it deletes that draft and nothing else. A track that was ever published keeps its row, because its columns and its status live on in Airtable; the program's four original tracks are published from the moment a site exists, so none of them is ever offered it.

Starting a track

Two ways, each ending on the new track's page, as a draft.

  • New track asks for the three things two tracks can never share: the Name, the Airtable status and the Key, the short word on the chip, plus the Learn course link when the track follows one. A name, status or key another track holds is refused, even when that track is a draft, since publishing the draft would claim it. With a link, the course's lessons are listed beside the questions, and the name is taken from the course when it is left empty. The chip color is chosen for you, the first one no other track holds, drafts included. The form starts empty; the questions are added on the track's page.
  • Duplicate copies every question of an existing track, the four original tracks included, and asks for a name, a status and a key of its own, refused as New track's are when another track holds them. The copy starts with no Learn course, no hours target, no partners and no partners' narrative; set them on its page. This is the usual way to start a track that resembles one you run: duplicate the 150-hour track and change what differs.

With a Learn course link filled in on New track, the lessons appear under the groups that are their modules, and each lesson offers Add a question under this lesson, which is how a form gets built lesson by lesson.

The track's page

The properties come first: Name, Airtable status, Key, Learn course, Hours target and Key chip color, which is one of blue, cyan, teal, green, red, pink or purple. The hours target may stay empty. After the chip color, Partners offers the sponsors Approved at the Partner tier today plus any the track already names, ticked, so a lapsed one stays until you untick it. Under them, Partners' narrative is one text for all of the track's partners, up to 5,000 characters, which you rewrite each term: when a partner's annual report is drafted, which the site does the day after that partner's term ends, its block for this track starts with the text as the track was last published, so after rewriting it, publish the track before the next partner's term ends. Each report keeps its own copy, edited on the report: a report drafted before a change keeps the words it started with, and Regenerate keeps them too. Save the track saves the properties; the questions save themselves as they are added, edited and moved. Save refuses a name, status or key another track holds, drafts included, and a refused Save draws the boxes again as you left them.

The Learn course row shows what the link resolved to, the course's title and number. Read the course again asks Learn afresh; otherwise the site keeps a day's reading, so a lesson renamed on Learn shows up here within a day. When Learn cannot be reached, the link the track already has is kept with a warning, the lessons cannot be listed, and the track still saves and publishes. A new link is not taken while Learn cannot be reached, and the notice says so; the box keeps the link you typed, so pressing Save the track again once Learn answers takes it.

Changing the link to another course matches every question that carried a lesson against the new course's lessons by its heading. Only a lesson's first question carries the lesson's title as its heading, so the other questions of that lesson follow it; only the questions of a lesson none of whose questions matched are left with no lesson. The notice names the questions matched and the ones that no longer point at a lesson.

Then Questions, by group: Total hours, Onboarding, Project and Wrap-up, the four parts of the Student Report Card's form. Total hours holds one question, Hours, which students see as the hours box. Any other question goes in Onboarding, Project or Wrap-up: the question screen offers Total hours to Hours alone, and Save and Publish refuse anything else. On a track with no Learn course, students see the hours box in a section of its own, My hours.

Each question is a row with what the student reads, its Airtable column and its control, and beside it Edit, Move up, Move down and Remove. The arrows move a question at once; if the site cannot keep a move, the question goes back and a notice above the list says why. Remove takes the question off the form; the column, and whatever students wrote in it, stay in Airtable, and the confirmation says so.

Since 1.123.58 a track that cannot be saved lists every problem at the top, each linked to its field, and a track another Administrator saved after you opened it is not overwritten; your own question moves on the same page do not count as a change. A Publish or Take off meanwhile is not a save, so it does not block yours. Publish, Check and Take off can be pressed once. A question moved while the connection failed is put back, and the page says so.

Each group ends with Add a question: the Airtable column, what the student reads, the control and, when the group's module has lessons Learn answered, Under lesson. Total hours offers it only while the track has no Hours question. Adding opens the new question's page.

When the track follows a course, the lessons of each group's module are listed under the group's questions, with a count such as Lessons on Learn: 3 of 13 have questions. Each lesson names the questions that report on it, or offers Add a question under this lesson. A question added that way is placed after the lesson's last question, carries the lesson, and takes the lesson's title as its heading when it is the lesson's first question.

A line above the questions says what publishing would create in Airtable, This track needs no new Airtable columns. or Publishing will create 3 columns in Airtable., and how long ago the base was read.

Controls and columns

Ten controls: Text, one line; Text, many lines; Rich text; Web address; Email address; Number; Checkbox; One choice of several; Screenshot; Contribution team. The control decides the Airtable column type: a new column is created with the type the control needs, and a column that already exists has to be of that type, or the publish screen refuses.

A duplicated track shares its columns with the track it came from, and the question's page says so, naming every other track that writes the column. Rewording a shared question keeps the column. Changing its control, or the choices of a select, gives it a column of its own, named after the track, which can still be renamed until the track is published. On a question no other track shares, changing the control keeps its column and changes only the type the column needs.

One question

Each question has a page of its own: the column and the control at the top, then the rows that apply to that control.

The certificate code question uses Filled in by the program. On the tracks that give a certificate code, an Airtable automation writes the code into the student's record, and the student copies it into the course's final lesson quiz. With the setting ticked, the Student Report Card shows the question's words, then the code as text the student can select and copy, then the help; before the code arrives, the words and the help alone. Nothing on the card can change it: a save leaves the cell as the automation wrote it, so a page opened before the code arrived can no longer empty it, and a typed or cleared code is never sent. That holds for an Administrator filling in a report on a student's behalf too, so a wrong code is corrected in Airtable. The card reads the record through a cache of up to five minutes, so a code written a moment ago can take that long to show. The setting changes no column, so it can be ticked on a question that has been published; students see the change once the track is published again.

Save the question returns to the track. A refusal redraws the question with what was typed, and the reason.

Once a track is published, its questions are locked: the column, the control and the choices are fixed, because the column in Airtable holds what students wrote, in that shape. The words can still change. To ask something differently, remove the question and add a new one with a column of its own.

Preview and History

Preview draws the draft's form as a student sees it: empty answers, no student's record, the same renderer and the same stylesheet as the Student Report Card. Nothing typed there is kept. The hours box sits where the Student Report Card puts it: with the button that opens the course when the track has a Learn course, side by side on the student's page and one under the other here in wp-admin, and on its own when the track has none.

History has three parts: what publishing would change, the published copy against the draft; every save, newest first and at most twenty, with who saved it, when, and what changed since the one before; and the publish log, every publish, unpublish, switch, column created and checklist item ticked, with who and when.

Publishing

Publish opens the publish screen. Nothing happens until the button at the bottom is pressed; the screen first reads the base and says what it found.

  • This track cannot be published yet lists what stops it: a column in Airtable with a question's name but another type, a control that cannot have a column created for it, a table that would pass Airtable's limit of 500 columns, a status, key or name another track holds, a draft's included, a question other than Hours in Total hours or Hours in another group, and a Students Reports table setting that holds anything but the table's ID, its name for example. Check it against Airtable refuses the same way while that setting is wrong.
  • Worth knowing before you publish lists what does not stop it: a choice of the Status column on Students Reports or Students that nearly matches the track's status but not exactly, which the syncs would never match; a Learn course link that does not resolve; a table past 450 columns. A choice that is missing altogether is not a warning: the third checklist item below says, for each table, whether it has the choice yet.
  • Columns: every column the track writes to, and whether it exists or will be created. With a schema token, the optional second token on the Connection tab of WPCredits Program > Settings, the site creates the missing columns when you publish. Without one, the screen lists the exact columns to create by hand, name and type, and Publish waits until the next reading finds them.
  • What the site cannot do: the three Airtable steps no token can take, with the exact values to use. Add the status to the condition of the automation Add students to Students Reports and Feedback; create the track's welcome email automation, as each of the four tracks has one; add the status as a choice of the Status column on both tables. Tick each with I have done this once it is done, and the tick records who and when. An unticked item never blocks publishing, but until the automation item is ticked, students cannot be put on the track from the institution import, because they would never get a report row.
  • Publishing any track adds its status to Currently mentoring in Settings, unless it is there already. The four original tracks' statuses are there from the start, so publishing one of them adds nothing new. A Settings save that would take a live track's status out saves everything else, leaves Currently mentoring as it was, and names the track.

When publishing would create columns in Airtable, Publish comes with a box: type the track's name exactly as it is written, then press the button. Capitals count; spaces around the name do not. The site can never remove a column it created, so a press whose text is not the name creates nothing and says so. The name confirms the columns the screen lists: if the columns publishing would create change before the button is pressed, nothing is published and the screen comes back with the new list to read and confirm again. With nothing to create, Publish is one press; a press that finds columns gone from the base since the page was drawn creates nothing, and the screen comes back to show them.

Publishing runs its steps one at a time and records each. If Airtable refuses part-way, the notice carries Airtable's own message, and pressing Publish again picks up at the first step not done. If the page stops part-way instead, because the server gave up on a long run, the columns made so far are already recorded, but for up to twenty minutes Publish on every track says another track is being published. After that, press Publish again: it creates only the columns the base still lacks, and the log names every column the site made.

What goes live is the track as it stood when Publish was pressed. An edit saved while Publish runs, in another tab or by another Administrator, is not part of that publish: the track then shows Unpublished changes until Publish the changes is pressed.

After publishing, the same screen offers Check it against Airtable, which reads the base again and says whether every column is still there with its type and the status is a choice on both tables, and, for every track but the program's four original ones, Take it off the live site. The four never offer it: a line beside the other actions says the program's original tracks always run, and to edit the track and publish the change instead. Unpublishing any other track is refused while any student holds the status, with the count; otherwise the track becomes a draft again, nothing in Airtable changes, and the status stays in Currently mentoring: removing it there takes the Student role from everybody on the track, which is a decision of its own.

Editing a published track's words makes it Unpublished changes; students keep the published copy until Publish the changes is pressed.

The four original tracks

The 150-hour, 50-hour, Developer and Designer tracks are the program's own four. Each has run from its definition in the Track Builder since 22 September 2026, and there is nothing left to switch between: no hand-written form and no plugin update can move one of them, and you edit, duplicate, preview and publish them exactly like a track you make yourself.

A fresh site seeds and publishes all four at once, with their publish checklist already ticked, from the seed files the plugin ships, so the program runs on day one with nobody pressing Publish. If one of the four is ever missing, wp wpcredits seed_tracks on the command line puts it back; a fresh site runs the same step by itself on the first page load after the plugin is installed.

Their statuses and keys belong to them. No other track can take the Airtable status or the key of one of the four, whether you are starting a new track, duplicating one, or saving one you already have: the refusal names which of the four original tracks keeps it. And the four cannot be deleted or unpublished at all; if something about one of them needs to change, edit the track and publish the change instead.

A site already on an earlier version upgrades once, on its first load after 1.116.0 arrives: nothing for you to press, and a load that is cut short partway is finished by the next one. On a fresh site a seeding cut short leaves no half-made track behind, and wp wpcredits seed_tracks puts back any of the four that is missing, then as at any other time.

Need help?

WPCredits Program > Tools > Need help? The question box over the WordPress documentation: its settings at the top of the screen, then how answers are produced, with the provider and the sites it is told to use, and a box for trying a question as somebody on the program would ask it.

Settings

At the top of the screen, a form with its own Save settings. One sentence says what the question box is, and its Details fold says where each question goes: the provider does the searching, so nothing is stored on this site, and each question, and the pages found for it, go to that company.

  • Need help? - its box, Switch it on, is on by default. Off means the box answers nobody, the header button disappears and the page it lives on is unpublished. Nothing is deleted, so switching it back on restores all of it.
  • Where answers come from - the provider searches wordpress.org, make.wordpress.org, learn.wordpress.org and developer.wordpress.org itself. Nothing is copied to this site, so there is nothing to configure and nothing to refresh.
  • Answer provider and Provider API key - leaving the provider as None keeps everything on this site and means there are no answers at all. Choosing one sends each question, and the extracts that match it, to that company. The key is stored in the database and never sent back to the browser; left blank, it keeps the current key. A key for the Gemini provider is free at aistudio.google.com.
  • Model - typed, gemini-flash-latest by default: the provider lists no models to choose from, so the field holds whatever model is saved. Leave it as the default unless you have a reason not to. It is an alias that always points at the current Gemini Flash, so it cannot be retired out from under the site.
  • Who can ask - mentors and administrators by default; optionally students and institutions as well, anybody logged in, or administrators only. Never anybody logged out, whatever this says. The documentation describes running the program rather than being on it, which is why students are not included by default.
  • Questions per person per hour - from 0 to 200, 20 by default, so a free tier cannot be spent in an afternoon. Past the limit, people are asked to come back shortly. 0 removes the per-person limit; the whole site can still be answered at most 300 questions a day.

While it is switched off, a notice above the section says so, with a link down to the switch; while it has no provider, the Provider row under the section says so, with a link back up. Its card on the Tools screen says which of the two it is, never the Airtable connection, which Need help? does not use. And a question that cannot be answered for want of a provider, a working model or a valid key tells the person asking that an Administrator can put it right in the Settings section of the Need help? screen, under WPCredits Program > Tools.

Who can read what

Every post and page carries a Program access control in the editor sidebar.

The levels come from the roles, so there is one per audience plus the two ends:

A level is read by any account holding the capability its row names, whatever its role. A post's author can always read it, at any level.

The levels do not nest. A mentor holds the mentor capability and nothing else, so a mentor cannot read a Student-level page. That is why documentation written for mentors has to repeat what students are told rather than link to it.

Gating is applied in four places, so there is no back way in: front-end listings filter restricted posts out, direct URLs send logged-out visitors to the login form and logged-in ones to an explanation, the rendered content and excerpt are filtered, and the REST API is filtered too.

Program updates and announcements

The Program updates and announcements column, in the Resources section near the top of both the Student Report Card and the Mentor Report Card, lists up to five recent posts from the Updates category, filtered by the same access levels. Each card lists Public posts and posts at its own level; the Student and Mentor Report Cards also list Students and mentors posts, so a post set to Mentor level appears on the mentor's card and on no other. Set the access level on the post and it lands in the right place; there is nothing else to configure.

The Administrator Dashboard's column lists private posts too: a post in Updates whose visibility is Private and whose access level is Administrators only appears there for the Administrators, and on no other card. The biweekly site update is one. A private post is never emailed to the site's subscribers or shared outside the site, which is why the update is private rather than published.

An update for sponsors, at the Sponsor level, opens for an Administrator in the Sponsor Dashboard's frame, as it does for a sponsor. Opened from Program updates while viewing a sponsor, its menu and the list beside it keep that sponsor.

Viewing a page as its owner

The Student Report Card, the Mentor Report Card, the Institution Dashboard and the Sponsor Dashboard each open, for an Administrator, with a switcher above the page whenever there is more than one to choose from: Viewing as student, Viewing as mentor, Viewing as institution or Viewing as sponsor. Pick a name in it and press Show to open that person's or that organization's page. Only Administrators are shown the switcher, and the note with it says so.

The switcher is one field, showing the name you are viewing until you pick another. Click it, or press Down, and the whole list opens under it, with the name in the field highlighted. The list runs A to Z without regard to capitals or accents, so Álvaro is among the A's, with numbers read as numbers, so Student 2 comes before Student 10, and with a space before any letter, so Teo Polytechnic comes before Teodora School. Type in the field and the list narrows to the names that hold what you typed, anywhere in the name and again without regard to capitals or accents, so "alvaro" finds Álvaro, with the first match highlighted; the field's placeholder, Find a student, Find a mentor, Find an institution or Find a sponsor, shows while it is empty. Up and Down move through the list, and Home and End go to its first and last names. Press Enter, or click a name, to pick it: the field shows it, and Show opens its page; picking alone opens nothing. Click the field again, press Escape or Tab, or click anywhere else, and the list closes with the name you picked last back in the field. When no name matches, the list says so. Come back to a page with your browser's Back button and the field shows the name that page is about, which is the one Show opens. Enter in the field never sends the form, and a screen reader hears how many names the list shows. In a browser running no JavaScript the field is not shown, and the plain sorted list works on its own.

The details card on an institution's page

At the head of the Representatives and agreement module on an institution's Institution Dashboard, above the people who act for it and its Collaboration Agreement, is the card Your institution's details, with the line "What the program has on record." It is drawn to every account of an institution whose agreement is settled and to an Administrator on any institution's page, opened through the switcher or reached as the page you land on. An institution whose agreement is not settled has no card: its accounts see the agreement panel alone, where they set its name on the agreement document.

The details read as rows under two small headings, in this order. Contact and agreement: the contact person, their role, who signs the agreement, their title, the languages the students study in, and the institution's page about WordPress Credits. Name and address: the name, the website, the city, the country and the contact's email. A detail the program holds nothing for reads "Not given yet".

Under each list a closed section opens the form for that group alone, with the application's own questions, labels and help, and the application's rules:

  • Correct these (saved at once) is under the first list. Saving writes the contact person to the Institutions table in Airtable and to the program records here, and the other answers to the institution's record on this site. It adds a line to the institution's history that names the details changed and none of their values, emails the people Who is emailed about institutions names what changed, from what to what, and says "Your institution's details are saved."
  • Ask to correct these (an Administrator checks first) is under the second. A member's press on Send to an Administrator writes nothing: it raises a request, shown on the Administrator Dashboard's Requests from institutions card, emails the same people with a link to it, and says "Sent: an Administrator checks the change, and you will see it here once it is decided." An Administrator is drawn this second form as Correct these (saved at once), with Save the details, as the first: their press saves at once, in either form, and emails as a save does, since an Administrator is the one who checks, and nobody approves their own change. While the school's request waits, an Administrator is offered no second form either: under the second list they read "A request from the school is waiting. Decide it in Requests from institutions on the Administrator Dashboard.", linked to that card while the page is published, and a post of that form is refused with the same sentence. The first form stays open to everyone allowed.

Below the two lists the card has a Tracks part, and for Administrators an Assigned Administrator part after it. Its row Tracks offered gives the tracks it offers that the site runs, by name, or "None listed yet.". It is set by Administrators alone. An Administrator is drawn a checkbox for each track the site runs, Save tracks, and the line "Students are asked which track they want when two or more are ticked."; an account of the institution reads the list and "The program sets the tracks your institution offers. To change them, write to" the program's contact address, with no form. A save adds a line to the institution's history: "Tracks offered were set:" and the names, or "Tracks offered were cleared.". The list is kept on this site and never written to Airtable. A track unpublished in the Track Builder drops out of the list and of the question, and comes back, still ticked, when it is published again. With two or more ticked, the registration form at /student-registration/ asks a student of the institution "Which track would you like to join?", required, with the ticked tracks and Not sure yet; with fewer, it asks nothing. The answer is written to the Students table's Requested track column (the track's name as the student saw it, or "Not sure yet") and shows under Answers and consent on the Registrations tab. If the column is missing, the row is written without it and the registration says it was left out. The answer is a request: an Administrator still assigns the track, and Status stays empty.

While a request waits, every account of the institution reads, under each row it would change, "Waiting for an Administrator:", what was asked and the day it was asked, with Withdraw it; an Administrator reads the same lines without the button, since the request is decided on the Administrator Dashboard. The second list then offers no form, because an institution has one request at a time. A second account, or a second tab, that asks meanwhile is told "One change is already waiting for an Administrator." and nothing is made. Once the request is decided, every account of the institution reads its outcome until the next request is sent: "Updated on" and the day after an approval; "An Administrator did not make the change you asked for" after a decline, with a colon and the Administrator's note when there is one; nothing after a withdrawal. Withdraw it brings the account back to this card.

A form posted with nothing changed says "Nothing was changed." and sends no email; a value posted back as it was drawn is not a change, even one the program holds in a form the application would not accept. A refused post gives back what was typed, with the problem under the field that has one, and a text that WordPress would take words from is refused whole, as on the application. If Airtable refuses the contact person's save, nothing is saved on this site either, the typed values come back, and the card says "The program records could not be updated, so nothing was saved. Try again in a while." The card never names Airtable to the institution.

A save at once is made under a lock of the institution's own, the option wpcpm_req_lock_details_<record> its request is raised under, with what the program has on record read again under it. Two tabs, or two accounts, posting the same correction save it once: the second is told "Nothing was changed." and writes, emails and records nothing. A save that finds the lock held, and a request sent while it is held, is told "Someone else is saving your institution's details at this moment, so nothing was done. Try again in a moment.", saves or makes nothing, and gives back the typed values; "One change is already waiting for an Administrator." is for a request that truly waits. The forms leave every rule to the site, so a box the browser would refuse, such as a stored contact's email that holds two addresses, does not stop a post of the rest.

A student's card on an institution's page

An institution's accounts open a student's card from the roster, and an Administrator opens the same card through the switcher. The card shows the student's name and program, whether they have signed in yet, the internship dates and cohort, the field of study, the tutor, the WordPress.org profile, the contribution teams and the personal website, then the mentor, the Student Report Card (read only, fetched when it is opened) and a link that downloads the student's details and course grades as a CSV file.

A mentor is optional in the program, and a student without one reads as normal. The Mentor row says "No mentor yet", in the roster's words, and the Mentor email row is left out, since there is nobody to write to. A mentor known by name and not by address keeps the row, which then reads "Not set". The card asks for no mentor and offers no way to ask for one.

Under the Student Report Card, a closed section named Correct this student's details holds the form that corrects five details: the name on the Student Report Card, the full name, the start date, the end date (at most a year after the start) and the field of study, which must be one of the program's own choices. It is shown to every account of the student's institution and to an Administrator, and to nobody else; a student with no progress record yet has no Student Report Card and no section. Saving writes to the program records at once, through a live read that places the student with the institution, and adds a line to the institution's history. When a value is refused the section names what was refused and says whether the rest was saved, and the form comes back with what was typed and not saved, for the account that typed it, while what was saved shows as the program records now hold it. The section opens by itself when the last save left something to say, so its sentence is not hidden in a closed section. Nothing on this card asks for a mentor or keeps notes. A mentor request already on record is still on the Administrator Dashboard's Requests from institutions card, where an Administrator closes it as before.

The For Administrators section of an institution's page

At the foot of an institution's Institution Dashboard, under its sections and above the line that says when its records were last read, an Administrator is shown For Administrators, with the line "Only Administrators see this section." It is drawn on any institution's page, opened through the switcher or reached as the page you land on. Nobody who acts for the institution sees it, or anything in it, whatever state their agreement is in. It holds two folded cards.

From the application lists the answers the institution's application gave that Airtable has no column for, each under the question it was asked: the contact's role, the languages the students study in, who will sign the agreement, their title, and the institution's page about WordPress Credits. They are kept when the application is approved and stay after the application itself is removed. An institution approved before 1.123.29 has none, and the card says "Nothing kept from the application."

History lists the latest 100 things that happened to the institution, newest first. Each row gives when, in the site's date and time formats; who, as the account's name, "The site" when the site did it itself, as when an invitation expires, or "A removed account" when the account is gone; and what happened, in a plain sentence. It covers the institution's members and invitations, with the address each invitation went to, its application and its agreement from the template being generated to a revoke, which also gives the note it was revoked with after "Note:", its details (the corrections it saved, and its requests to correct them), its requests, its imports, the changes made to its students, and the roster's refusals; a line about a note on a student, if the history holds one, reads "A note about a student was added." or "A note about a student was deleted." When there are more than 100, the card says "Showing the latest 100." An institution with nothing recorded says "Nothing has been recorded for this institution yet."

A row reads in today's words whatever the day it was written. A member row names the account as it is called now, "A former member" when the account is gone, says that it was added as a member or is no longer one, and then says how it joined or left in the words of the People card ("Added by an Administrator", "Joined by invitation", "Their access was removed", "They removed their own access"), never the code the row was stored with. A request that was closed is worded by what became of it: "An Administrator closed a request as handled.", "An Administrator declined a request.", "An Administrator approved a change to the institution's details." or, for one taken back, "The institution withdrew a request." (or "An Administrator withdrew a request." when an Administrator withdrew it), with the Administrator's note after it when the note can be shown, and the outcome alone when it cannot. A school's request to correct its details reads "The institution asked to correct its details.", and a correction it saved "Details were corrected:" and the names of the details. A line written before the Administrators were named is read in the words used now.

Arranging the Student Report Card

Under a student's profile and mentor columns the Student Report Card is a stack of up to six modules: Your first weeks (for a new student only), Program updates and resources, My course (My hours when there is no course to open), Report form and feedback forms, My mentor call, and Tools from our sponsors when its setting on the Sponsors tab of Settings shows it and the student has offers or claimed tools. A module with nothing to show is left out and has no arrows. Each carries two small arrows at its top right, and pressing one moves the module up or down at once, the way the block editor moves blocks. The order belongs to the student: they arrange their own card, and it stays as they left it. When you open a student's card through the switcher you see their order and can arrange it for them with the same arrows; there Tools from our sponsors is at most one line, saying how many tools they claimed. Nobody else sees the arrows.

A student's or a mentor's own language

At the top right of the Student Report Card and the Mentor Report Card, above the title, a student or a mentor sees a small language switcher: the flag and the name of the language the page is in. Pressing it opens a short list, and pressing a language there keeps it; the page comes back in that language, and the emails the site sends that person are in it from then on. The choice is kept on their account, where WordPress keeps an account's language, and is theirs alone. Administrators are never shown the language switcher, on their own page or on a page they open for somebody else, and you read the page in your own language.

The list holds only the languages the plugin has a translation for, each named in itself, with the site's own language first. While there is no translation the switcher is not shown at all, so nothing changes on a site that has none. Translators are given what students and mentors read, so a sentence only an Administrator, an institution or a sponsor sees stays in English, and so does anything not translated yet. A language whose translation a later version takes out goes back to the site's language by itself.

There is no setting. A translation arrives with a version of the plugin, and the language is on the list from then on. Dates and WordPress's own words follow too once that language is installed under Settings > General, in the Site Language list (installing it does not change the site's language). A flag is the flag of the country the translation is written for; a language that belongs to no one country is listed by its name. Where a system draws no flags (Windows), the country's two letters stand in its place.

Arranging an institution's page

The Institution Dashboard is three sections, each with two small arrows at its top right, named after the section, for example "Move Students up". The order belongs to the institution and is the same for everyone who signs in for it. When you open the page through the switcher you see that institution's order and can arrange it for them with the same arrows, and your move is theirs from then on. A section with nothing to show is left out and has no arrows. Only the institution's representatives and Administrators are shown the arrows; a tutor sees the page in its order but cannot move anything.

The Sponsor Dashboard has nothing to arrange since 1.123.78: it is drawn in the dashboards' frame, with a menu down the side and a view for each of its parts, Overview, Your sponsorship (while "Sponsor tiers" is on), Offers, Students reached, Mentors to sponsor, Your company and Agreement, each at its own address. Opened through the switcher, it keeps the sponsor you chose as you move between views, and the switcher keeps the view when you choose another sponsor. Its Sponsor guide and the updates a sponsor reads open in the same frame for the people who act for a sponsor; you read the Sponsor guide there too.

Group sessions, from a student's card or a mentor's

On a student's card, opened through the switcher, the group sessions they are on are listed under My mentor call, and each one that has not started offers Take them off the session. It asks first, then takes the student off, gives their place back and emails them a file that takes the session out of their calendar, as their own Leave the session would.

On a mentor's card you can change or cancel their group sessions as they can. When you move one, the mentor is emailed as well as the students on it, with an invitation that moves it in their calendar.

Running it day to day

The sync

The students and the mentors syncs read Airtable and reconcile accounts: create what is missing, update what has changed, and apply the two settings under When someone leaves (Settings, Students and mentors tab) to the rest: When a mentor is no longer active and When a student leaves the program. Run one by hand from the Students or Mentors screen, or leave Automatic sync on - students and mentors every three hours, half an hour apart.

They start half an hour apart on purpose. The student rows carry what students and mentors are shown on their cards, so a stale copy is a stale card, and it is the expensive half of the pair: it reads one WordPress.org profile per mentor, cached for twelve hours, while building the mentor cards. The mentors run reads three Airtable tables and makes no WordPress.org request. Two runs in the same request would be one long request. A run still going when the next one is due is left to finish rather than restarted.

Syncs every three hours (1.98.2). All three Airtable syncs - students, mentors and institutions - share one three-hour clock, and the first runs are staggered so each starts at its own point in the cycle: students half an hour in, mentors an hour, institutions an hour and a half. WordPress cron runs each event at or after its scheduled time, so the cadences drift apart after that and on a busy site two can still land close together, each safe behind its own lock. Before this only the students sync ran every three hours and the other two ran once a day, which meant an institution changed in the base was a day old on the site. Nothing has to be switched off and on again for the change to take: on the first request after the update each sync sees its own event still on the daily schedule, clears it and puts it back on the three-hour one. The housekeeping jobs are not syncs and stay daily - the three application retention runs (institutions, sponsors and mentors), the two agreement discards, the nightly reminder of agreements waiting, invitation expiry, the semester report drafting and the ceiling's sweep - because the settings behind them are in days and a base that is down must not stop a file being forgotten on time. The Mentor Status Checker is not a sync either: it reads WordPress.org profiles rather than Airtable, and its automatic run is daily (weekly until 1.122.4).

A correction made while the institutions sync reads (Institutions release 2). A school's details corrected on the site, on its Institution Dashboard or by an Administrator's approval of its request, are written to Airtable and then to the site's copy of the Institutions table, one correction at a time, under the option wpcpm_institutions_index_lock; a correction that cannot take it within a second is in Airtable and reaches the site with the next run. The institutions sync writes that copy whole from what it read of the base, so a run that read before a correction could put back the value it replaced. A correction made while a run holds its lock therefore asks for one more run five minutes later, which reads the change from the base. Only one such run waits at a time, and it keeps to Automatic sync and leaves a run still going alone.

Since 1.123.56 the institutions sync says on Slack that an institution has joined. A run that finds a record at Confirmed the site has not announced before posts one message once it has finished: the institution's name, its city and country where the record holds them, the Administrator it is assigned to where it has one, and a last line with how many confirmed institutions that makes. It goes to the Slack webhook saved for the Mentor Status Checker, so the channel is chosen in Slack, and nothing is sent or recorded while no webhook is saved. Up to three in one run are announced one by one; more than that is one message naming them all, because a stage column edited in bulk is not fifty pieces of news. Each institution is announced once, under the option wpcpm_institution_announced, and the first run that has a webhook records every institution already at Confirmed and says nothing, so the partnerships signed before this shipped are not announced as new. A confirmation the program dated more than thirty days ago is history rather than news: it is remembered without a word, so a list of older partnerships entered in the base is quiet, while a record whose Confirmed on is empty or cannot be read is announced, losing a real partnership to an empty field being the worse of the two mistakes. A test institution is announced nowhere and is left out of the total the message prints, as it is left out of every other figure the site draws; renamed away from TEST, it is news at the sync that makes it real. A message Slack refuses leaves its institution unannounced, so the next run says it again, and the message is in the site's language whatever language the run was started in.

Accounts are matched by the Airtable record the sync stored, then by email address. Since 1.123.58 a mentor whose WordPress.org username is an account's login, with nothing else to tie the two, is not linked: the match waits under Needs confirming on the Mentors screen's Sync tab. A match you confirm is linked and given the Mentor role (an Administrator's account keeps its roles); with Invitation emails on it is also sent the invitation with the welcome, unless the account was an active mentor already, is an Administrator's, or its invitation is held. The next completed run removes a waiting match whose mentor has left the base. Needs confirming is the sync's path only: an application's activation still links an account by the applicant's own username. No account is ever deleted by a sync - the most it will do is remove a role.

The sync report on each screen says what happened rather than only that it finished: created, updated, skipped and why.

Since 1.122.33 the mentors sync makes and links its accounts through the same step that making a mentor from an application uses, so there is one way to make a mentor: it matches as above, lists an account matched by username alone under Needs confirming, for an Administrator to confirm, and makes an account only when none matches. An application has no record id yet, so its lookup is the address, then the username, then the profile an account holds. The sync leaves a mentor made from an application alone while that mentor's Mentors row is not written (see Applications to mentor): it does not revoke the account while the row is not written. If the sync itself links the account to an Active row, that ends the wait, and the account is treated as any other mentor's. Nor does a run revoke a mentor who was made one, or whose row was written or found, after the run began; the next run reads the row and decides. The Mentors screen's Sync tab says how many wait.

Since 1.123.42 the mentors sync also sends the welcome to a mentor whose account already existed. It used to queue the invitation, which carries the welcome, only for an account it created, so a returning mentor, or a student or an institution member made a mentor, was linked and given the role and never received it. With Invitation emails on, a run now queues it for each account it makes an active mentor that was not one before: the account had no Mentor role, or held it with its active flag off. A mentor who is active already, whether the sync or an application made them one, is not sent it again by a later run, so each is welcomed once each time they become active. An Administrator's account is never sent it. An account matched by username alone is not linked by the sync: it waits under Needs confirming on the Sync tab, and Confirm there decides whether it is welcomed. An account whose invitation is held already is named in a notice and left as it is. A run that would welcome more than five accounts at once, a base changed in bulk, sends none: it holds each one's invitation on the Mentors screen's Accounts tab, and names them all in the first notice of its report, so Send invite on a row sends the welcome to the ones that should have it. The Last sync report counts those it queued under Invitations sent to existing accounts.

Since 1.123.62 the mentors sync also keeps the public list of active mentors on the site. For each active mentor it stores the name, the WordPress.org profile, the country, the languages and whether the mentor is sponsored, and no address. In the base Country and Languages are links to tables of their own, so the sync reads those tables' names as well. The list is replaced only by a run that read the whole Mentors table and could name every country and language: a run that stops halfway, or cannot read one of the linked tables, leaves the last list as it is and says so in a notice of the Last sync report. Who sponsors a mentor is not stored with the list. It is read from the sponsors' own records, the mentors each Approved sponsor holds on the Sponsors screen, never a test sponsor's, so a change there shows at once. The Credits Program Mentors plugin, which draws the directory on the mentors' page, reads this list (the filter wpcpm_public_mentors) and reads no Airtable of its own. The list is as fresh as the last finished run: a mentor made Active in Airtable appears on the page after the next one.

Since 1.123.58 the mentors and students syncs count before they take anyone's role. A run that read no records, or fewer than half as many as there are accounts linked to a record, stops before its revoke step and keeps every account; the Sync tab says what it read and offers Run anyway, and wp wpcredits sync_mentors --accept does the same on the command line, for that run only. A stopped run is not running: the Sync tab stops polling, prints why in the progress panel with a line to reload the page for Run anyway or Cancel, and Cancel ends a stopped run too. A passing refusal from Airtable makes every sync wait and carry on. Pressing Sync students now or Sync mentors now while a run is going comes back with "A sync is already running. Its progress is shown below." and starts nothing; wp wpcredits sync_mentors --restart starts again on purpose. While a run goes, a screen reader hears each step, a stall and the finish, and the finished run's counts are said on the Sync tab for the mentors and students syncs; the institutions sync says accounts created only.

Two commands go with the Mentors row an activation writes. wp wpcredits mentor_airtable_row <reference> prints the row an application would write, each cell as its column takes it and what would be left out, and writes nothing; it reads Airtable and prints the applicant's answers, so it is for a test application. wp wpcredits mentor_airtable_row --check --email=<address> is for the launch, run by hand before Make mentors from applications is switched on: it writes one synthetic row to the Mentors table, with the address given and the Status Inactive, which neither the mentors sync nor the Mentor Status Checker reads, reads it back, deletes it, and says which columns the base kept. It deletes only the row it wrote, it changes nothing on the site, and it ends in an error while a row may be left behind, which then has to be deleted in Airtable by hand, and while a column did not take what the site sends.

Since 1.123.58 wp wpcredits setting get <key> prints a setting as the screen shows it, a secret masked, and wp wpcredits setting set <key> <value> [--dry-run] changes one by the Save's own rules: it prints what changed, what it would change with --dry-run, or why the value was refused; everyone is the value that sets a Who is mailed list to every Administrator account. Change a live setting one way at a time: a settings tab open in a browser keeps its own view of the page it drew.

Since 1.123.61 wp wpcredits start_pages makes the Start here page (/start-here/) and the Team Matcher page (/find-your-team/) the way the first-week checklist's switch does, and prints each page's ID and address. A page that already exists, at its address or in its stored ID, is kept as it is. The Team Matcher page is made only while the Find Your Team plugin's quiz block is available; the command says so when it is not, and can be run again once the plugin is active. Run it on a site where the switch was turned on before the Find Your Team plugin was active.

Invitations

An invitation is a password-reset link. Send them in bulk by switching Invitation emails on before a sync, or one at a time from the Students and Mentors screens and the Accounts tab of the Institutions and Sponsors screens - which is the safer habit, because a first sync creates around ninety accounts at once. On those four lists you can also tick several accounts and choose Send invite or Resend invite under Bulk actions: those are queued and go out a few at a time.

Each invitation cancels the link in the one before it, so only the newest email works: somebody who opens an older one is told the link appears to be invalid. For the same reason a second invitation to the same person within fifteen minutes is not sent, on purpose. Resend invite on a person's row says so and sends nothing, and so does a second press made while the first is still sending; Resend invite on ticked accounts leaves out anybody invited in the last fifteen minutes and says how many it left out; and a bulk send passes over anybody invited in the last fifteen minutes or being sent one at that moment. Ask them to use their newest email, or send another once the fifteen minutes are up. An invitation the mail host refuses does not count as sent: Resend invite on the row says the mail host refused it, the fifteen minutes do not start, and the lists still show the last invitation that did go, or none, as a bulk send that meets a refusal leaves them too, its card counting how many it did not send. "Not sent" there covers anybody the mail host refused, anybody another press was sending one to at that moment, anybody invited in the last fifteen minutes, an account deleted before its turn, and anybody whose invitation is held until an Administrator confirms the account; the Emails tool's Log shows each refusal. That last invitation's link no longer works, though, since the refused attempt made a new one: send another once the site's email is working.

Since 1.122.33 the mentor's invitation carries the welcome a new mentor is sent, after the invitation's own lines: the two Start here posts, one welcoming mentors to their Mentor Report Card and one welcoming students to their Student Report Card; the five student courses on learn.wordpress.org (the WordPress Credits Translation Track since 1.122.38), which a mentor joins through each course's invitation link to see what is asked of their mentees; the program's private Slack channel for mentors; the discount codes for students' tools, which are in that channel; the mentor resource folder; and the sign-off. The courses' invitation links and the folder's link are private, and are not in the plugin or in this guide: the shipped text holds one bracketed line where they go, and the mentor coordinator types them into the template, Invitation: mentor in Tools > Emails, before any mentor is sent it. A saved edit of that template is sent in place of the shipped text, welcome or none, so an edit saved before the welcome existed has to be replaced, and an edit saved before 1.122.38 keeps its own course list: the mentor coordinator adds the line for the WordPress Credits Translation Track, and the track's invitation link, to that edit. A reply to the invitation reaches the address under Contact address in emails, as the program's Reply-To, which no other invitation carries.

The mentor's invitation is queued on every activation of a mentor application, whatever Invitation emails says, and goes out a few at a time like the others, under the same rules: the fifteen minutes, the lock, and a refused email writes no stamp. It is not queued for an Administrator, and it is held when the account is not yet confirmed as the person's, linked by WordPress.org username alone or with another account also answering for the applicant: Send invite or Resend invite on its row in the Mentors screen's Accounts tab sends it once an Administrator has confirmed which account is the person's. The Activated view of the Mentors screen's Waiting for review tab says what became of it since the person was made a mentor.

Since 1.122.30 an institution sends a student's welcome invitation again itself. On a student's card on the Institution Dashboard, a student with no sign-in on record since the site began recording sign-ins, on October 15, 2026, shows a line saying so, with when their last invitation was sent or that none has been, and a Resend invitation button (Send invitation when none has). Every member of the student's own institution can press it, and so can an Administrator who opens that institution's dashboard through the switcher. It sends the same invitation as Resend invite here, with a new link that replaces the one before, and no Administrator is emailed. A student with a sign-in on record shows no line and no button: a lost password has WordPress's own reset. A student who also mentors, whose invitation was held when an application made them a mentor, shows the line with no button: in its place the card says the program's Administrators send this invitation once they have confirmed the account belongs to the student, and a press from a page drawn before is told the same and sends nothing, taking none of the day's twenty. The institution learns only whether a sign-in is on record, never when.

The fifteen minutes hold here too, and each institution can send twenty a day, the presses of an Administrator through the switcher included. Two presses for one student at the same moment send one invitation: the second is told what a press within the fifteen minutes is told. A press that sends nothing takes none of the day's twenty, an email the mail host refuses included, and a refused email does not start the fifteen minutes either. The card then says the invitation could not be sent and that the link in any earlier invitation no longer works, and asks the school to try again in a few minutes and to write to their program contact if it fails again; its line still names the last invitation that went, though that one's link no longer works. Each send is in the Emails tool's Log, which keeps its rows for 30 days, and the institution's history records each one in its audit log, with who pressed it and whether as a member or as an Administrator. Those rows are listed in the History card, in the For Administrators section of the school's Institution Dashboard, which shows when each happened and who pressed it.

Who follows an institution up

An institution's assigned Administrator is its contact at the program. It comes from the areas of responsibility under Settings > Institutions; once the areas are set, the Countries table in Airtable no longer decides who follows a school up. A school gets its Administrator on approval of its application on this site, from the institutions sync when it was added in Airtable, from the seed command, or on its details card. A school in a country no area covers stays unassigned until an Administrator assigns it on its details card.

  • On an application. A new application takes the Administrator of its country's area, or of its region's, and that Administrator alone is emailed, with a link to it ("Institution assigned, to the Administrator" in WPCredits Program > Tools > Emails). An application no area covers is assigned to nobody, and then it is emailed as it always was: to the addresses in Who is emailed about institutions on Settings > Institutions, or to every Administrator when that is empty. An application with an assigned Administrator who is still an Administrator goes to them alone, even if that email fails: it is never sent to those addresses in its place, and the application is marked so you can see the email did not go. An application held for review or caught as spam sends no Administrator an email. The setting still decides who is emailed about everything else an institution does, such as agreements, requests and members leaving.
  • On approval. The institution is given the Administrator the application had, unless it already has one or was set to Nobody. An application that had none, or whose Administrator is no longer an Administrator, takes the area's Administrator at that moment, if there is one. Nobody is emailed by the approval.
  • Added in Airtable. A school added in Airtable after the seed, by a form, an automation or by hand, is given its area's Administrator by the next institutions sync, and that Administrator is emailed as on a reassignment. The sync assigns only a school it had not read before, never one that has an Administrator or was set to Nobody, and nothing on its first read or after the stored list of institutions was rebuilt. It sends at most five of these emails a run; a school past them is assigned without one. A test institution is assigned without the email. When more than ten schools are new in one read, none is assigned, so an Administrator assigns them on their details cards. Each assignment is written to the school's history.
  • Reassigning. On the institution's details card, under Assigned Administrator, open Change who follows it up, choose an Administrator (or Nobody) and save. The new Administrator is emailed, unless they made the change themselves, and the card says they were emailed only when the email was sent. The change is written to the institution's history.
  • Where it shows. The queues on the Institutions screen say "Assigned to" and the name, or that nobody is assigned. The Administrator Dashboard's application card says "Assigned to" too. The school's Institution Dashboard shows the assigned Administrator as its contact, with their booking link.

Only accounts with the plugin's manage capability can be assigned. A person who stops being an Administrator stays on the record until somebody else is chosen, but is nobody's contact.

Seeding the areas and the assignments once. wp wpcredits institutions_seed fills in what R1's screens read from the site, from what Airtable holds today. Run it with --dry-run first: it writes nothing and prints a summary of what a run would do, school by school for what it cannot assign, and says why. A real run prints the same summary and asks "Write this to the site?"; --yes skips the question.

  • It reads three Airtable tables and changes none: Institutions (name, country, and the Airtable column that records who first handled the institution), Team Members (name, email, booking link) and Tutors.
  • It gives each country the Administrator whose account has the address of its contact in the Countries table. Regions are left empty: set them afterward on Settings > Institutions. When the site already holds areas, it writes none and assigns by the areas it finds.
  • It keeps each Administrator's booking link from the Countries table's contact, or from Team Members for the person who first handled a school, and only while the account has none, and assigns each institution to its country's Administrator, or else to the Administrator that column names. While the site holds no areas, a country's contact with no matching Administrator account is named in the summary with the countries it leaves without an Administrator; a person from Team Members who matches no Administrator is named with how many institutions stay unassigned for them. A booking link that is not an https address is not kept, and the summary names the Administrator.
  • It adds each school's tutors from the Tutors table to the school's tutor list, except a tutor somebody removed from that list on this site. A tutor linked to a record the site does not hold is named in the summary and not added.
  • It never replaces an area, a booking link, an assignee or a tutor already listed, or a school set to Nobody, so it can be run again. It sends no email: nobody is told of an assignment it makes, and no tutor is invited. A school whose record somebody else is changing at that moment is not assigned: the command names it and ends with an error, and running it again assigns it.
  • With no countries map yet, it says to run the institutions sync on the Institutions screen's Sync and storage tab first.

The Tutor level and the tutor list. An invitation has a Level. A Representative works the page; a Tutor only reads it: the students, their Student Report Cards and the semester reports. A tutor is shown no button that changes anything, and a request that tries to change something is refused and writes nothing. A tutor of a school whose agreement is not yet accepted sees nothing but what a stranger sees. Each level has its own invitation email, and Resend keeps the level.

Separately, each school keeps a tutor list: the names its students pick from in the Tutor box when the school enrolls them. It lives on the site, in the Tutors section of the People card, where a representative or an Administrator can Add a tutor (a name and an email address) and Remove one. Adding a tutor to the list sends no email and makes no account; removing one leaves their account and their past students as they are. A tutor who accepts a Tutor invitation is added to the list. The enrollment form and the tutor box read this list, never Airtable.

Pages the plugin owns

Activation creates the Student Report Card and Mentor Report Card pages and gates them. If one goes missing, re-activating the plugin recreates it, and the Students or Mentors screen says the page is missing. A Settings row that switches on a page, such as an application form's, says the same of its page. The institution application form's page is at /institution-application/ since 1.123.27, titled "Bring WordPress Credits to your institution", moved once from /apply/ on the first request after the update (its slug, title and content each only while still the plugin's own), and /apply/ takes a visitor there. The Administrator guide's page is at /administrator-guide/ since 1.123.41, moved once from /program-manager-guide/ on the first request after the update (its slug alone, and only while it is still the old one and no other page, post or attachment holds the new one: the title, the content, the status and the modified date are not touched, and no save runs), and /program-manager-guide/ takes a visitor there. The release script writes the page by its ID, so a release does not care which address it has.

The student registration form's page is at /student-registration/ since 1.123.54, with the same Welcome text the Airtable form opened with, the program's address and the form. Activation makes it, and so can a person, with the same address: a published page at that address is used as it is, and nothing on it is changed. The page is not gated, because the students who use it have no account yet, and it is not cached.

Since 1.123.63 the registration form's line for a student whose institution is not on the list leads to the institution application page on this site while it is published, and says to get in touch otherwise. It used to lead to the Students Interest Form, which is kept on Airtable; the site's public pages now link to no form there.

Since 1.123.64 the site has a student interest form, for a student whose institution is not in the program yet. The plugin makes no page for it: an editor adds the Student Interest Form block, or the [wpcpm_student_interest] shortcode, to a page, and the site remembers that page as pages are saved. The page is not gated and not cached. Each interest is kept on the site as one private record: the student's answers, the representative's name and address, the two sentences the student agreed to with the policy's address, what the form's checks noticed, and who last changed its state and when. Nothing is written to Airtable. A spam interest is deleted 30 days after it was marked as spam and a closed one 365 days after it was closed, by a daily job; the others stay until an Administrator moves them. Deleting the plugin removes every interest, the page's ID and the daily job, and leaves the page. While the form is open and its page is published, the registration form's line for a student whose institution is not on the list leads to it, and to the institution application otherwise.

The Institution Dashboard's guide button follows a published page at institution-guide on this site when there is one, and the handbook's institutions page until that page exists. The Sponsor Dashboard's guide button follows a published page at sponsor-guide on this site when there is one, and the handbook's sponsor guide until that page exists. Each release republishes both pages from the built Institution guide and Sponsor guide, so a change made to either page by hand lasts only until the next release. The Mentor Report Card's guide button follows a published page at mentor-guide on this site in the same way, and the handbook's Mentor guide until that page exists. The handbook keeps what is for people who are not mentors yet: who can become one, the mentor badge and how to apply. The Student Report Card's guide button does the same with a published page at student-guide and the handbook's Student guide. The handbook keeps what is for people who are not on the program yet: which institutions take part, the interest forms and how to apply.

Uninstall

Uninstall removes the settings, the sync state, the access-level meta, the last sign-in and last visit the site records for every account, and the custom roles, and moves affected accounts back to Subscriber; it also deletes the sponsors' offers, pools and locks, and the claims meta, the sponsor applications with the logo files nobody approved, the mentor applications with what deleted ones counted for the public feed of their figures, the sponsor reports and their locks, forgetting the PDF each report held, the sponsor events with the people on them and their locks, and the institution records, which hold the five answers an application gave, the assigned Administrator, the tutor list and the tracks, and the student registrations with their answers and consent evidence, their locks and the page's ID. It also deletes the first-week checklist's start time and each student's own ticks, and the IDs of the Start here and Team Matcher pages (the pages themselves stay, as every page the plugin makes does), and the quiet students' daily list, the time the switch last went On, the week of the last Monday email, the run's lock and its place on the clock, and from every account the stamps of the last report save, the last edit seen in Airtable, "We've already talked" and the last reminder. Accounts are never deleted, but the program details the plugin stored on them (record IDs, program, mentor links, availability, sign-in times) are removed.

When something is wrong

Semester reports

The site drafts a report for each institution semester once the semester has ended and every student in it is finished, or 45 days after the end (the "Drafting grace" setting) if some are not. The job runs nightly and drafts at most ten reports a run; it never drafts a semester that ended before the feature was installed, so older semesters are drafted by hand with the Draft now button on the Institutions screen's Semester reports tab. Each draft is mailed to the addresses in "Who reviews reports", or to every Administrator when that is empty.

Review a draft on the Institution Dashboard, reached through the switcher from the Semester reports tab. Edit the narrative, choose the quotes, then press Approve this report. The institution sees the report from that moment, with a Download PDF button, and its accounts are mailed; an institution with no account is not mailed and the screen says so, so send the PDF by hand. Reopen for editing takes the report back to a draft and out of the institution's view. Approval is refused while the students' consent answers cannot be read.

The Administrator Dashboard

The Administrator Dashboard at /administrator-dashboard/ is the page to start the day on. It is gated to Administrators. Since 1.123.69 it is drawn in the dashboards' frame: a top bar with Education Directory, a Homepage link and your photo and first name with Log out behind them (when the theme leaves the page to the frame; otherwise the theme's own header shows above a slim bar with the Menu button), a menu down the side, and a main area as wide as the window. The menu holds the page's views: Overview, where the page opens, with the number of decisions waiting beside it; Watch, its own view since 1.123.71, with the number of cards to watch that have something to look at; Cohort timeline; The program (called Reference before 1.123.71); and, since 1.123.71, Program updates, which opens the newest of the program's updates when there is one. Each update opens in the same frame, with the other updates listed down the right of the page, newest first, the one you are reading marked; on a narrow screen the list sits under the update's title, folded behind Program updates. Under In wp-admin it links the Students, Mentors, Institutions, Sponsors and offers, Tracks, Tools and Settings screens, each marked as leaving the page, and the Mentors item counts the mentor applications waiting. Under Help come the Ask box, which sends your question to the program's assistant when it is set up, the Administrator guide, the WordPress Credits handbook and the program's Slack channel. Since 1.123.70 this guide opens in the same frame, with the same menu, and lists its sections down the right of the page: the section you are reading is marked and shows its parts, and the list stays in view as you scroll. On a narrow screen the list sits under the guide's title, folded behind On this page. Collapse menu at its foot folds the menu to its icons, and the browser remembers it. On a tablet the menu shows its icons alone, a dot on an icon where something waits; on a phone it opens from the Menu button and closes with Close menu or Escape. In a right-to-left language the menu sits on the right.

What it is for. The site is the working layer on top of the program data. Airtable is the system of record for students, mentors and institutions for now: the site reads their records from it, writes back to it, and turns them into something people can use without asking an Administrator first; the sponsors' records live on this site. Students see their own Student Report Card and fix their own details. Mentors see who they are responsible for, publish their availability, and are flagged when someone goes quiet. An Administrator sees all of it in one place, plus the things only an Administrator should touch. The page is where you:

  • check the cohorts' health at a glance instead of opening records one by one: the head, the line on each card, and Programs running, which counts the students in progress per track and per institution;
  • triage the students who need a call, are ending soon or are on track: each mentor's Mentor Report Card sorts their students into those three groups, and you open it through the switcher, while Programs running shows how many of each institution's students are waiting for a mentor and when their internships end;
  • review the mentors' status and approvals: Requests from institutions holds what the institutions asked for, each mentor's status is on the Mentors screen, and the Mentor Status Checker moves a mentor from Vetted - positive to Active once their WordPress.org profile shows they completed the Credits Mentor's Course;
  • keep the numbers that feed the public program dashboard current: Syncs and health says which sync needs a look, and Duplicated students how many students the Student Duplicate Finder's last scan found with more than one row in Airtable.

The head and the figures. The Overview opens with how many decisions wait for you, the sum of every queue below, and how long the oldest has waited and in which queue ("The oldest has waited 67 days, in Semester reports."), with Review the oldest, which opens that card, or for the mentor applications the Mentors screen's Waiting for review tab. With nothing waiting it says "Nothing waits for you today". Under it come the program's figures, with the homepage's definitions: the share of students who graduate rather than drop out and the share of graduates who would recommend the program, while the homepage shows them, then the active mentors, with how many signed in during the last 30 days, and the programs running, with at how many institutions; one line says when the two shares were read, and that the mentors and programs are as of today. A count in the menu, an age on a row and a state on a cohort tile are one mark, the homepage's status tag: words in the status's tint and border, never a colored edge.

The cards. A card folds and unfolds with one press on its row. The number beside a title is how many things it holds, and the words after it say where it stands, so a folded card still tells you what is in it: "2 waiting", "1 offer under its threshold", "3 duplicated students as of September 28, 2026", "Every audience's sync ran in the last six hours". Each card with a home in wp-admin links the tab that holds its items, Open on the Institutions screen, Open on the Sponsors screen or, on Mentor engagement, Open the Mentors screen's Engagement tab: as the last line of its body while it is open, and beside its row while it is folded (under the row on a narrow screen). The institutions' cards open the Institutions screen's Waiting for review tab, and Semester reports its Semester reports tab. The sponsors' cards open the Sponsors screen at the tab that holds their items: Sponsor applications, Sponsor posts to review, Sponsor offers to review, Events and Sponsor Collaboration Agreements each at its own card on the Waiting for review tab, Offers running low at Offers and codes, New interests at Interests, Sponsor reports at Reports, and Sponsor terms ending and Sponsors at the Sponsors tab, where a Sponsor terms ending row's sponsor opens its Edit form. Institution applications says how many it left out: under the fifty oldest open applications it lists, a line says how many more are waiting, listed here as these are decided, and under its fold of rejected and spam applications, how many more it keeps. Each application's title opens it in the Institutions screen's queue, its state is said in that screen's words (such as "new" or "waiting on the applicant"), and an application the anti-spam checks held carries a note to open it on the Institutions screen to read which checks. Sponsor applications, Sponsor posts to review, Sponsor offers to review and Sponsor Collaboration Agreements each list the fifty oldest in their queue, and while more are waiting, a line under the list says how many more, listed here as these are decided. None of these lines links anywhere, and a card's link to its screen comes last, under them. For those four sponsor cards the number beside the title, the words after it and the head count everything waiting in the queue, the number the Sponsors screen shows for it: the applications in full, at any size, and the posts, the offers and the agreements up to 200, past which they read 200+, as their cards on the Sponsors screen do. Duplicated students keeps its own button, Open the Student Duplicate Finder, in its body as well as beside its title. The rows of Syncs and health each carry their own Open link to their sync's screen instead, since no one screen holds the audiences' three syncs and the outcome figures' weekly read. A link in a mail and the way back from a decision each open the card they land on.

Waiting for you holds what needs an Administrator's decision: Institution applications, Collaboration Agreements, Semester reports, Requests from institutions, Sponsor applications, Sponsor posts to review, Sponsor offers to review, Events while Sponsor tiers is on, Sponsor Collaboration Agreements and Sponsor reports.
